original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Reduce exact modular row arithmetic in the complete fixed h=6 stage-pair certificate by skipping proved-zero prefixes, preserving all output fields, rank fallbacks, source checks and cache decisions.
scope_change_reason: An originally posed replay-runtime experiment on the complete historical h=6 caller. The modular elimination has a finite known-zero prefix after each pivot. The prior mathematical results are cited, not audited as the deliverable.
bottleneck_link: A small verification-throughput improvement. The profile identifies modular elimination as a minor component; the headline is exact redundant arithmetic removed, with complete runtime measured separately.
stop_rule: Ship the first verified elimination-work reduction. Do not optimize matrix subtraction, rational rank, source construction, cache policy or any other path.
evidence: verify.py and adapter.py: full byte-identical scientific payload, identical 65536-entry cache workload, live rank comparison, reference bytecode multiplication count, independent minor oracle and boundary/arithmetic controls. benchmark.py measures complete alternating fresh processes without a timing threshold.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Would the same zero-prefix optimization pay off in another explicitly pinned modular-rank caller?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The current full caller is dominated by rational matrix operations, so an arithmetic reduction need not yield a stable wall-time gain.
open_questions.first_step: Profile a named complete caller and establish its input, source and cache contracts before applying the kernel.
open_questions.blocked_by: No other caller, shared-code integration or broader runtime gain is certified here.
